care.label: CARE + G.E.T.
care.note: The library's native format. Context, Action, Result/Format, Example, plus Generate -> Explain -> Test.

co-star.label: CO-STAR
co-star.note: Splits CARE's Result into Style/Tone/Response and promotes Audience to its own slot. Lossless.

tidd-ec.label: TIDD-EC
tidd-ec.note: The only common format with an explicit DONT slot, so anti-fabrication and data-safety rules land naturally.

risen.label: RISEN
risen.note: Strong for multi-step work. No Example slot, so the worked example is lost.

crispe.label: CRISPE
crispe.note: Its Experiment slot asks for alternatives rather than verification, and there is no Example slot.

race.label: RACE
race.note: Compact four-slot format. Keeps guardrails and audience; drops the worked example and the whole G.E.T. validation step.

rtf.label: RTF
rtf.note: Minimal. Fine for a quick one-off; strips every verification and safety rule.

ape.label: APE
ape.note: Purpose-led and very short. No role, audience or example.

bab.label: BAB
bab.note: Persuasive narrative shape. A poor fit for deliverable prompts - use it to pitch the work, not to produce it.

chat.label: Compact chat
chat.note: One paragraph for short-context chat boxes. Deliberately lossy.

prompts.name: Refinement Session Pack
prompts.audience: Squad members attending refinement; product owner deciding priorities
prompts.task: Prepare the refinement session so every minute goes to decisions, not reading. Draft the pack. Flag stories not worth refining yet (too vague, blocked) with what must happen first.
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira

prompts.name: Showcase & Retrospective Pack
prompts.audience: Showcase: stakeholders and sponsor. Retro: the squad
prompts.task: Prepare the showcase narrative and turn retro inputs into actions that actually land. Draft both. In the retro analysis, distinguish what the squad controls from what needs escalation.
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira
PASTE TEAM NOTES / SURVEY IF ANY

prompts.name: Master – Agile Ceremony Facilitation & Support
prompts.audience: The squad (developers, testers, product owner) and attending stakeholders
prompts.task: Support and contribute to sprint ceremonies so the squad stays aligned and informed: prepare refinement sessions, support sprint planning and goal setting, and support showcases and retrospectives. Produce on request
modes: refinement session prep (candidate stories with open questions, assumptions and dependency notes; DoR check per story)
sprint planning inputs (prioritised backlog summary, capacity check, draft sprint goal options)
showcase pack (storyboard, demo scenarios in business language, anticipated questions)
retrospective support (theme analysis of my notes, candidate actions with owners, follow-through check on last retro's actions)
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira

prompts.name: Story Map from a User Journey
prompts.audience: Squad (build sequencing) and stakeholders (scope conversations)
prompts.task: Build the story map: backbone, stories, walking skeleton and release slices. Draft the map. List the assumptions you made about journey order and persona goals for me to verify.
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira

prompts.name: Feature Slicing & MVP Definition
prompts.audience: Product owner (scope decisions) and squad (build)
prompts.task: Slice the feature vertically, define the thinnest valuable slice, and set MVP/MMP boundaries. Draft slices and MVP. Mark compliance-driven items that cannot be descoped regardless of value logic.
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira

prompts.name: Master – User Story Mapping & Slicing
prompts.audience: Squad and product owner; story map doubles as a stakeholder communication artefact
prompts.task: Decompose features into thin, valuable vertical slices: build story maps around the user journey, slice features vertically, define the MVP/MMP, and write acceptance criteria with concrete examples. Produce on request
modes: story map (backbone of user activities left-to-right, stories beneath by priority, walking skeleton marked)
slicing options for a feature (each slice: value delivered, what's deliberately excluded, dependency notes) with a recommended sequence
MVP/MMP definition (in/out with rationale per item)
acceptance criteria with Given/When/Then plus concrete example data
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira
DESCRIBE THE USER JOURNEY OR FEATURE
LIST — e.g. case officer, customer, field officer

prompts.name: Story Elaboration to Definition of Ready (with BDD)
prompts.audience: Developers and testers picking the story up; product owner confirming intent
prompts.task: Elaborate the story to genuinely Ready: rules, criteria and BDD scenarios a developer and tester can work from without re-asking. Elaborate, then run the DoR checklist over your own output and state pass/fail per criterion.
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira

prompts.name: Spike Definition & Outcome Record
prompts.audience: Squad (running the spike), product owner (accepting the decision)
prompts.task: Define a sharp spike before it runs, and turn its findings into a decision record afterwards. Draft whichever half I ask for. Reject spike questions that are really two questions — split them.
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira

prompts.name: Master – Just-in-Time Requirements Elaboration
prompts.audience: Squad (build and test from the stories), product owner (readiness decisions)
prompts.task: Progressively elaborate requirements on cadence so stories are ready ahead of each sprint: manage Definition of Ready compliance, elaborate just-in-time (right detail now, defer the rest), and run spikes for uncertainty. Produce on request
modes: readiness assessment of pasted stories against the DoR (met/not met per criterion, blocking gaps, who can close each)
story elaboration (description, business rules, acceptance criteria, BDD example scenarios with data)
'now vs later' analysis — what detail is needed this sprint vs deferrable
spike definitions (question to answer, timebox, done-means, decision the outcome feeds)
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira

prompts.name: Release Plan & Scope Sequencing
prompts.audience: Product owner and stakeholders; roadmap consumers
prompts.task: Draft a release plan that unlocks value earliest and survives contact with dependencies. Draft the plan. Show one alternative sequencing and why you rejected it.
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira

prompts.name: Sprint Capacity & Dependency Inputs
prompts.audience: Squad and product owner in sprint planning
prompts.task: Prepare the capacity and dependency inputs that make sprint planning a 30-minute decision. Draft the inputs. Flag overcommitment explicitly if candidates exceed capacity — do not quietly stretch the numbers.
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira

prompts.name: Master – Iteration & Release Planning Support
prompts.audience: Product owner and delivery lead (decisions); squad (commitment); stakeholders (roadmap view)
prompts.task: Support iteration and release planning by shaping scope, sequencing and sprint goals: release scope options, capacity and dependency inputs, and roadmap alignment with explicit trade-offs. Produce on request
modes: release scope options (what each release contains, value delivered, sequencing rationale, risk)
sprint plan inputs (candidate scope vs capacity with buffer, draft sprint goal options, DoR status)
dependency register for the plan (dependency, type, owner, needed-by, risk if late)
roadmap view and trade-off records when dates move
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira

prompts.name: Flow & Bottleneck Analysis
prompts.audience: Squad (owns the fixes) and delivery lead
prompts.task: Find where work actually gets stuck, and test whether the data supports the squad's intuition. Run the analysis. Where the data contradicts the squad's felt pain, say so and explain the gap.
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira
PASTE CYCLE TIME PER STAGE / CFD EXPORT / TICKET TIMESTAMPS
WHAT THE SQUAD SAYS IS SLOW

prompts.name: Delivery Forecast with Confidence
prompts.audience: Delivery lead and stakeholders asking 'when will it be done?'
prompts.task: Forecast when the remaining scope will complete, as a defensible range. Produce the forecast. If my history is under 4 sprints, say the forecast is low-confidence and what to do instead.
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira
PASTE THROUGHPUT/VELOCITY PER SPRINT, LAST 6+ SPRINTS

prompts.name: Master – Agile Metrics & Flow Analysis
prompts.audience: Squad and delivery lead primarily; summarised views for stakeholders
prompts.task: Analyse velocity, throughput and flow to inform forecasting and delivery improvement: track velocity and burn, find bottlenecks, and produce forecasts with honest confidence ranges. Produce on request
modes: velocity/burn analysis (trend, variance, drivers — scope change vs estimation vs interruptions)
flow analysis (where work waits, WIP vs limits, cycle time by stage, bottleneck hypothesis with evidence)
delivery forecast (range with confidence, method stated, assumptions listed, what would change it)
improvement suggestions tied to the specific bottleneck found
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira
PASTE VELOCITY HISTORY / CYCLE TIMES / CFD DATA / THROUGHPUT — OR DESCRIBE WHAT JIRA CAN EXPORT
E.G. 'WILL WE HIT THE SEPTEMBER RELEASE?'

prompts.name: Definition of Ready / Done Uplift
prompts.audience: The squad, who must own and apply it every sprint
prompts.task: Draft an uplifted DoR and DoD that would have caught the recent failures, sized to the squad's maturity. Draft both definitions. For each recent failure I gave, point to the criterion that now catches it — and admit any failure your draft still wouldn't catch.
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira
E.G. STORIES BOUNCED MID-SPRINT, DEFECTS FROM UNCLEAR CRITERIA

prompts.name: Improvement Backlog & Experiments
prompts.audience: The squad; delivery lead sponsoring the time
prompts.task: Turn improvement themes into a prioritised backlog of small experiments with clear success signals. Draft the backlog. Reject vague improvements ('communicate better') — restate each as a concrete, trialable change.
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira
PASTE RETRO THEMES / PAIN POINTS / METRIC SIGNALS

prompts.name: Master – Agile Ways of Working Uplift
prompts.audience: The squad (owners of their ways of working); Lead BA/practice interested in patterns
prompts.task: Embed and improve analysis practices within the squad: uplift Definitions of Ready and Done, improve how analysis supports flow, and run continuous improvement that actually sticks. Produce on request
modes: DoR/DoD drafts tailored to the squad's context and pain points (each criterion: what it means, why it's there, how checked)
analysis ways-of-working guidelines (how analysis feeds the flow: elaboration cadence, BA involvement per ceremony, artefact expectations)
practice gap analysis from my description (gap, consequence seen, candidate practice, effort)
improvement backlog with experiments (hypothesis, trial period, success signal)
inputs: SQUAD NAME, PRODUCT/SYSTEM, CADENCE e.g. 2-week sprints, TOOL e.g. Jira
PASTE EXISTING DoR/DoD/WORKING AGREEMENTS IF ANY

prompts.name: KPI Definitions & Measures Table
prompts.audience: Benefit owners and the reporting/data team who must build the measures
prompts.task: Turn the listed benefits into a rigorous KPI definition table that reporting teams could implement without further interpretation. Draft the table, then list measurement risks (gaming, lag, data quality) per KPI.
inputs: PASTE BENEFITS STATEMENTS OR BUSINESS CASE EXTRACT

prompts.name: Value Realisation Assessment
prompts.audience: Sponsor and steering committee
prompts.task: Assess realised value against plan, explain variances, and recommend optimisation actions. Draft the assessment (max 2 pages equivalent). Where data is insufficient to judge a benefit, say so explicitly rather than inferring success.

prompts.name: Master – Benefits Realisation & KPI Management
prompts.audience: Benefit owners, the project sponsor and the PMO; summaries may be lifted into executive and board reporting
prompts.task: Act as my analysis partner for benefits realisation: define measurable benefits, design the KPIs and measures that evidence them, and assess whether value is actually being delivered, so the organisation can report outcomes credibly and identify optimisation opportunities. Produce, as I request them
modes: a benefits map linking initiative outputs to outcomes to benefits
a KPI definition table (KPI, definition, formula, baseline, target, data source, frequency, owner)
a value realisation assessment comparing actuals to targets with root causes and optimisation recommendations
inputs: LIST EXPECTED BENEFITS FROM THE BUSINESS CASE

prompts.name: Discovery Workshop Plan & Question Set
prompts.service: Business Needs Assessments (Initial and High Level Requirements)
prompts.audience: Workshop attendees (agenda) and the facilitating BA (question set and rationale)
prompts.task: Design a discovery workshop that elicits business needs efficiently and surfaces disagreement early. Draft agenda + questions, plus a 'facilitation risks' list (dominant voices, scope drift, sensitive topics such as team performance) with mitigations.

prompts.name: Raw Notes → Business Needs Statements
prompts.service: Business Needs Assessments (Initial and High Level Requirements)
prompts.audience: Stakeholders who will validate the needs; the delivery team consuming them downstream
prompts.task: Convert the raw notes into clean, attributed business needs statements ready for validation. Draft the table. Do not invent needs that lack support in the notes — flag gaps instead.
inputs: PASTE MEETING NOTES / TRANSCRIPT / EMAIL THREADS

prompts.name: Master – Business Needs Assessment
prompts.service: Business Needs Assessments (Initial and High Level Requirements)
prompts.audience: Business stakeholders and SMEs contributing needs; outputs feed the project brief and requirements backlog
prompts.task: Support end-to-end elicitation of business needs and high-level requirements: plan discovery sessions, generate strong questions, convert raw notes into structured needs statements, and expose conflicts and gaps between stakeholders. Support these modes on request
modes: workshop/interview plan with 8-12 questions sequenced broad-to-specific including conflict-testing questions
structure raw notes into business needs statements ('The business needs the ability to [capability] so that [outcome]')
simulate a named stakeholder so I can practise elicitation, then critique which questions I missed
inputs: PASTE ANY BRIEFS, EMAILS OR NOTES

prompts.name: Problem Statement & Opportunity Assessment
prompts.audience: Sponsor and investment governance
prompts.task: Produce a sharp problem statement and opportunity assessment that would survive challenge at an investment committee. Apply 5 Whys to my symptoms first and show the chain, then draft both artefacts. Mark every unquantified impact '[TO BE QUANTIFIED]'.
inputs: PASTE NOTES, DATA POINTS, COMPLAINTS, AUDIT FINDINGS

prompts.name: Business Case Inputs & Strategic Alignment
prompts.audience: Business case author and finance reviewers
prompts.task: Draft the BA-owned inputs to the business case: benefits, costs categories, alignment narrative and assumptions. Draft the inputs. Never fabricate dollar figures — provide the structure and mark '[FINANCE TO ESTIMATE]'.

prompts.name: Master – Discovery & Problem Definition
prompts.audience: Sponsor, business case authors and investment governance forums
prompts.task: Help me define the real problem and the case for change: separate symptoms from root causes, quantify impact, frame the opportunity, test strategic alignment, and draft business case inputs and initial risk assessments. Produce on request
modes: a problem statement (situation, impact, magnitude, consequence of inaction)
an opportunity assessment with options at a high level
strategic alignment assessment against the organisation's objectives
an initial risk list (risk, cause, consequence, likelihood, impact, mitigation)
inputs: WHAT PROMPTED IT — incident, audit, strategy, pain point

prompts.name: Data Requirements & Dictionary
prompts.audience: Data owners for validation; engineers for implementation
prompts.task: Produce a business data dictionary and requirements table for the fields in scope. Draft the dictionary, then list the top data-quality and privacy risks (e.g. health information exposure in reporting) with mitigations.
inputs: PASTE FIELD LIST, FORM, OR API EXTRACT

prompts.name: Reporting Requirements Specification
prompts.audience: Report consumers for validation; BI/reporting developers for build
prompts.task: Specify the reports and KPIs so a BI developer could build them without re-eliciting. Draft the specification for each report I describe. Challenge me where a report has no clear decision attached to it.
inputs: WHO NEEDS TO KNOW WHAT, TO MAKE WHICH DECISION

prompts.name: Master – Data & Reporting Analysis
prompts.audience: Business data owners, reporting teams and the data engineering team
prompts.task: Define the business data, information and reporting requirements for this initiative: what data is needed, what it means, where it comes from, and what reports and KPIs it must feed. Produce on request
modes: data requirements catalogue (entity, element, business definition, classification incl. personal/health info, quality expectation)
source-to-target data mapping tables
reporting requirements (report, purpose, audience, KPIs, dimensions, frequency, access restrictions)
KPI definitions

for data warehouse / BI work: a business question catalogue (what/why/how/when/who per question), MECE validation of question themes, business logic and refresh-frequency definitions, and BI technical specification structure (sources, joins, logic — flagged for peer review via validation queries)
inputs: LIST, e.g. core case management system, billing system, request intake channel, data warehouse

prompts.name: Defect Impact & Urgency Assessment
prompts.audience: Product owner and prioritisation forum; business stakeholders affected
prompts.task: Translate the technical defect into a business impact and urgency assessment that supports a prioritisation decision. Draft the assessment. Where impact data is missing, state what evidence would settle it.

prompts.name: Fix Change Assessment & Requirement Updates
prompts.audience: Delivery team, testers and the documentation owner
prompts.task: Assess the ripple effect of the fix and draft the updated requirements and end-state process narrative. Draft all three parts, then run a consistency check between the new requirements and the end-state process and flag contradictions.

prompts.name: Master – Defect & Work-around Analysis
prompts.audience: Product owner, support teams and the delivery team fixing the defect
prompts.task: Analyse the defect and its work-around from a business standpoint: impact, root cause hypotheses, options for resolution, and the flow-on changes to existing requirements and processes when a fix lands. Produce on request
modes: defect analysis (symptom, affected process step, business impact, urgency rating with rationale)
work-around assessment (steps, cost, risk, sustainability)
change assessment for the proposed fix (which requirements and process maps change, regression risk)
updated requirement wording and end-state process description

prompts.name: Feature & Functional Requirements Draft
prompts.audience: Stakeholders for sign-off; delivery team for build
prompts.task: Draft the feature definitions and numbered functional requirements for the pasted needs. Draft features, requirements and business rules. Flag every place you had to assume, as 'ASSUMPTION:' inline.

prompts.name: Non-Functional Requirements Elicitation & Draft
prompts.audience: Business owners (targets), architects and testers (verification)
prompts.task: Elicit and draft a measurable NFR set appropriate to a system of this type. Ask me the checklist questions I can answer now, then draft the NFRs from my answers. Do not silently invent targets — every unvalidated number gets the '[PROPOSED — VALIDATE]' flag.
inputs: USERS, PEAK LOADS, GROWTH IF KNOWN

prompts.name: Master – Functional Requirements Analysis
prompts.audience: Business stakeholders (validation), designers and developers (build), testers (verification)
prompts.task: Elaborate business needs into well-formed features, functional requirements and non-functional requirements across business and system layers, then quality-review them for ambiguity, testability, completeness and consistency. Produce on request
modes: feature definitions (name, description, business need served, in/out of scope)
functional requirements per feature ('The system shall...' with acceptance criteria)
NFR set covering performance, availability, security, privacy, accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA), auditability, usability
a quality review pass flagging vague words, untestable items and gaps with suggested rewrites
inputs: NEW BUILD / CONFIGURING PRODUCT / ENHANCEMENT — NAME SYSTEM IF KNOWN

prompts.name: As-Is Process Map (from description)
prompts.audience: Process performers who will validate it step by step
prompts.task: Convert my rough description into a structured as-is process map ready for stakeholder validation. Draft the map. List every step where my description was ambiguous or incomplete as targeted validation questions.

prompts.name: To-Be Design & Gap Analysis
prompts.audience: Improvement sponsor (decision) and delivery/change teams (planning)
prompts.task: Design the to-be process and quantify the gap from the as-is. Draft to-be and gap analysis. Respect my constraints — do not design changes to systems I flagged as fixed.
inputs: BUDGET, SYSTEMS THAT CANNOT CHANGE, POLICY/LEGISLATIVE CONSTRAINTS

prompts.name: Master – Process Analysis & Improvement
prompts.audience: Process owners and performers (validation), improvement sponsors (decisions), delivery team (implementation)
prompts.task: Analyse and improve the business process end-to-end: capture the as-is accurately, diagnose pain points to root cause, design a to-be that resolves them, and produce the gap analysis between the two. Produce on request
modes: as-is process narrative from my description with pain points annotated at the step where they occur
root cause analysis of key pain points
to-be process that addresses each pain point, with the change and its rationale marked per step
gap analysis table (as-is step, to-be step, change type, impact on people/process/technology, transition need)

prompts.name: Capability Assessment & Audit Report
prompts.audience: Executive sponsor of the assessment; the assessed area's leadership (so findings must be specific and fair)
prompts.task: Assess the capability of the business area against what it needs to deliver, and report gaps with uplift priorities. Draft the assessment from my evidence. Where evidence is thin for a rating, rate it 'insufficient evidence' rather than guessing.
inputs: PASTE INTERVIEWS, METRICS, SURVEY RESULTS, PRIOR REVIEWS

prompts.name: Decision Support Paper (Options Analysis)
prompts.audience: The decision forum (executives); written so a member who reads only page one can decide
prompts.task: Produce a decision support paper that lets the forum decide in one sitting: clear question, evidenced options, explicit trade-offs, recommendation with conditions. Draft the paper. Include a 'challenge' paragraph: the strongest argument against your own recommendation.
inputs: WHAT MATTERS — cost, risk, speed, capability, workforce impact

prompts.name: Master – Strategic Business Analysis & Advisory
prompts.audience: Executives and senior business leaders; secondary: strategy, portfolio and architecture teams
prompts.task: Act as my strategic-analysis partner for executive advisory work: assess internal capability, frame hypotheses and problems, support decisions with options analysis, assess organisational impact and strategic alignment, and develop business architecture views (capability models, value streams, operating model views). Produce on request
modes: capability assessment (capability, current maturity, evidence, gap, uplift priority)
hypothesis and problem analysis (hypothesis, evidence for/against, tests to run)
decision support paper (question, options, criteria, analysis, recommendation with conditions)
organisational impact assessment (people, structure, ways of working, operating model deltas)
strategic alignment analysis
business architecture views described in text and Mermaid diagrams (capability model, value stream)
inputs: WHAT LEADERSHIP HAS ASKED FOR — capability audit, decision support, costing, organisational impact, strategic alignment, business architecture
WHO — e.g. deputy CEO, divisional executive, CIO

prompts.name: AI Use Case Definition
prompts.audience: AI governance forum and the business owner
prompts.task: Define the candidate AI use case rigorously enough for a governance forum to assess it. Draft the definition. Challenge the use case where the value hypothesis is weak or a non-AI fix would do.
inputs: DESCRIBE — e.g. summarising case correspondence, triaging incoming requests, drafting field reports
DESCRIBE, FLAG PERSONAL OR SENSITIVE DATA

prompts.name: AI Guardrails & Evaluation Criteria
prompts.audience: Engineering (implementation), risk and governance (assurance)
prompts.task: Specify the guardrails, controls and evaluation criteria that make this AI use case safe to operate. Draft both tables scaled to the risk rating. Mark thresholds '[PROPOSED — VALIDATE WITH BUSINESS OWNER]'.

prompts.name: Master – AI Transformation Analysis
prompts.audience: Business owners, AI governance forum, and the engineering team building the solution
prompts.task: Shape AI-enabled solutions that are aligned to business objectives and governable: define use cases, agent capabilities, prompt/intent specifications, input/output contracts, guardrails and evaluation criteria. Produce on request
modes: AI use case definition and concept brief (problem, users, value/ROI hypothesis, human-in-the-loop model, risk rating with rationale)
AI suitability and assurance assessment against the applicable AI assurance framework, including whether rules-based automation is the simpler answer

agent capability and behaviour model (capability, inputs, outputs, tools/data accessed, trigger conditions, autonomy boundaries, escalation path to human, error handling when a data source is unavailable)
model selection requirements (accuracy vs cost vs latency trade-offs, cost per transaction)
prompt/intent specifications and grounding/RAG data requirements (knowledge sources, permissions, hallucination controls)
guardrails and controls (input filtering, output constraints, monitoring, human review points, consumption/cost controls for runaway tasks)
evaluation criteria and sustainability requirements (accuracy, safety, fairness thresholds; model drift testing and RAG refresh cadence; decision gates to refine, retire or scale)
inputs: DESCRIBE THE AI OPPORTUNITY OR CANDIDATE USE CASE

prompts.name: Epic → Stories Breakdown with Acceptance Criteria
prompts.audience: Scrum team (build and test) and product owner (prioritisation)
prompts.task: Break the epic into sprint-ready user stories with complete acceptance criteria. Draft the breakdown, then review your own stories against INVEST and flag any that fail, with suggested fixes.
inputs: PASTE EPIC DESCRIPTION AND ANY REQUIREMENTS

prompts.name: Backlog Refinement & Prioritisation Review
prompts.audience: Product owner and delivery lead
prompts.task: Review the pasted backlog for readiness and produce a defensible prioritisation. Deliver both tables and a short list of themes (recurring quality problems) to fix at the source.

prompts.name: Master – Agile Backlog Management
prompts.audience: Product owner, scrum team and stakeholders reading the backlog
prompts.task: Keep the delivery backlog healthy on cadence: break epics into features and stories, write acceptance criteria, refine and prioritise, and keep items meeting the Definition of Ready. Produce on request
modes: epic → feature → story breakdowns
acceptance criteria for pasted stories
refinement review of pasted backlog items flagging vagueness, missing criteria, oversized stories with suggested splits
MoSCoW or WSJF prioritisation with one-line rationale each. After drafting stories, self-critique for vague criteria and missing edge cases, then fix them

prompts.name: RFI/RFT Question Framework
prompts.audience: Vendors (questions) and the evaluation panel (guidance columns)
prompts.task: Draft the vendor-facing question framework that will elicit comparable, evaluable responses. Draft the framework. Flag any question that invites marketing rather than evidence, and tighten it.

prompts.name: Vendor Evaluation Scoring Matrix
prompts.audience: Evaluation panel and probity advisor
prompts.task: Build the weighted scoring model and comparative analysis structure for a defensible vendor evaluation. Draft the matrix and template. Sanity-check the weights against my stated priorities and flag mismatches.

prompts.name: Master – Procurement & Vendor Analysis
prompts.audience: Procurement team, evaluation panel, and delegates approving the recommendation
prompts.task: Support vendor selection and commercial decision-making across the procurement lifecycle: approach strategy, RFI/RFT content, market scans, pricing and licensing analysis, evaluation frameworks and recommendation support. Produce on request
modes: procurement approach comparison (RFI vs RFT vs direct, with rationale)
RFI/RFT question frameworks mapped to requirements
vendor capability criteria
pricing model and licensing analysis (perpetual vs subscription vs consumption; scaling scenarios)
weighted evaluation scoring framework
comparative analysis and recommendation structure

prompts.name: Transition Requirements & Readiness Checklist
prompts.audience: Readiness leads (execution) and go-live decision forum (go/no-go)
prompts.task: Define what must be true before go-live: transition requirements plus a verifiable readiness checklist. Draft requirements and checklist. Flag the items most commonly missed (access provisioning lead times, support knowledge articles, external party comms).

prompts.name: Showcase & Desk Check Pack
prompts.audience: Business SMEs and stakeholders attending; BA facilitating
prompts.task: Design the showcase session and desk check scripts that let the business validate the build against their needs. Draft both packs. Ensure scenarios cover the highest-risk and highest-frequency paths first, and say why you ranked them so.

prompts.name: Master – Operational Readiness & Transition
prompts.audience: Business readiness leads, support teams, change managers and the go-live decision forum
prompts.task: Elaborate the process and technology transition requirements and support change management so the business and support teams are genuinely ready at go-live. Produce on request
modes: transition requirements (process cutover, data cutover dependencies, access, training, support)
showcase/walkthrough session designs with scenarios to demonstrate
desk check scripts for business validation
system transition plan structure (phases, entry/exit criteria, rollback triggers)
operational readiness checklist with owner and evidence per item

prompts.name: Traceability Matrix Build & Gap Report
prompts.audience: BA and test lead (fix gaps); governance (assurance)
prompts.task: Build the traceability matrix from the pasted artefacts and report every gap. Build matrix and gap report. Do not force-fit doubtful links — mark them 'UNCERTAIN — CONFIRM' instead.

prompts.name: Decision Log Entries from Meeting Notes
prompts.audience: Governance forums and future team members needing the 'why'
prompts.task: Extract and formalise every decision into audit-ready decision log entries. Extract the entries. Where the notes imply but do not state a decision, put it in the 'not decided' table with a question to close it out.

prompts.name: Master – Requirements Governance & Traceability
prompts.audience: Project governance, auditors, and the delivery team relying on a single source of truth
prompts.task: Maintain control of requirements and decisions: traceability from business need through to test, a disciplined decision log, change control support and consistency checking across artefacts. Produce on request
modes: traceability matrix structure and population from pasted artefacts (need → requirement → story → test, with gaps flagged)
decision log entries from meeting notes (decision, date, decider, rationale, alternatives rejected, impacts)
scope creep review of new requests against the baseline (within scope / beyond scope / ambiguous, with recommended action)
cross-artefact consistency check flagging contradictions
inputs: LIST — needs, requirements, stories, designs, tests

prompts.name: BA Plan & Estimates
prompts.service: Sizing, Estimation, Dependency and Prioritisation Management
prompts.audience: PM (planning), resource managers (forecast), BA team (execution)
prompts.task: Draft the BA plan with estimated effort and an explicit assumptions log. Draft the plan. Challenge scope items that look under- or over-invested relative to their risk.

prompts.name: Dependency Map & Prioritisation
prompts.service: Sizing, Estimation, Dependency and Prioritisation Management
prompts.audience: Delivery leads and prioritisation forum
prompts.task: Map dependencies and produce a defensible priority order. Deliver map, diagram and prioritisation. Flag circular or fragile dependency chains explicitly.

prompts.name: Master – Sizing, Estimation & Prioritisation
prompts.service: Sizing, Estimation, Dependency and Prioritisation Management
prompts.audience: Project manager, delivery leads and resource managers
prompts.task: Support definition and prioritisation of requirements and BA work based on business and technical needs and dependencies: BA planning, estimation with explicit assumptions, dependency mapping and prioritisation. Produce on request
modes: BA plan (activities, deliverables, approach, estimate range, dependencies per phase)
estimation breakdowns with assumptions log
dependency map (item, depends on, type, criticality, risk if late) plus a suggested sequence
prioritisation using MoSCoW or value/effort with rationale and deferral risks

prompts.name: Solution Options Assessment
prompts.audience: Design authority / steering committee deciding
prompts.task: Produce an options assessment that makes the trade-offs explicit and recommends defensibly. Propose criteria and weights from my priorities, ask me to confirm, then assess. State every assumption behind a score.
inputs: LIST 2-4 OPTIONS WITH A LINE EACH

prompts.name: Regulatory & Policy Compliance Assessment
prompts.audience: Design team (remediation), legal/privacy advisors (confirmation), governance (assurance)
prompts.task: Assess the solution against each obligation and derive the business rules and requirements needed for compliance. Draft the assessment and rules. Mark every interpretation that needs legal/privacy confirmation.
inputs: DESCRIBE WHAT THE SOLUTION DOES, DATA IT TOUCHES
LIST — e.g. privacy legislation, legislation covering health or other sensitive information, information security standards, sector regulation, records legislation

prompts.name: Master – Solution Analysis & Design Support
prompts.audience: Solution designers, architects, design authority and business owners
prompts.task: Assess solution options and compliance needs so design decisions are made with clear business analysis: option assessments, regulatory and policy compliance assessments, and the business rules the solution must honour. Produce on request
modes: solution options assessment (criteria and weights, option scores with rationale, sensitivity check, recommendation)
compliance assessment (obligation, requirement it creates, solution behaviour, gap, remediation)
business rules extraction and categorisation (constraint / computation / derivation / inference) with ambiguity flags
inputs: PRIVACY / INFORMATION SECURITY / SECTOR REGULATION / ACCESSIBILITY / RECORDS — LIST KNOWN

prompts.name: Stakeholder Register & Engagement Plan
prompts.audience: BA and project leadership — treat as internally sensitive
prompts.task: Build the stakeholder register and a specific, actionable engagement plan. Ask me 3-4 questions about dynamics first, then draft. Flag likely missing stakeholders based on the initiative type (e.g. employee representatives, privacy officer, records management, delivery partners).

prompts.name: Workshop / Showcase Session Design
prompts.audience: Attendees (agenda) and facilitator (full design)
prompts.task: Design a session that achieves its stated outputs and keeps a mixed-attitude audience engaged. Draft the design. Note where resistant stakeholders need specific handling and how.

prompts.name: Master – Stakeholder Analysis & Engagement
prompts.audience: BA and project leadership using the plan; some outputs (comms) go direct to stakeholders
prompts.task: Identify contributing stakeholders and manage engagement and alignment: registers, interest/influence mapping, engagement plans, RACI, conflict resolution strategies and engagement communications. Produce on request
modes: stakeholder register (name/role, area, interest, influence, attitude, needs, engagement approach, cadence, owner)
interest/influence matrix with tailored strategies, alliances and risk flags
RACI for pasted activities with bottleneck checks (3+ Consulted, missing Accountable)
conflict resolution strategy for two named positions (underlying needs, 3 approaches, recommended talking points)
audience-tailored update messages. Ask me about organisational dynamics before mapping
inputs: LIST KNOWN STAKEHOLDERS/AREAS, INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL — e.g. operations teams, field staff, delivery partners, employee representatives, customer groups, IT, vendors

prompts.name: UAT Scenarios & Scripts from Requirements
prompts.audience: Business SMEs executing UAT; test lead tracking coverage
prompts.task: Produce UAT scenarios and step-by-step scripts business users can execute unaided. Draft catalogue and scripts. Then self-review: list requirements with thin coverage and edge cases you could not derive without more information.
inputs: NOTES — e.g. masked production data only

prompts.name: Requirements Validation & Coverage Review
prompts.audience: Test lead and BA (fixes); governance (assurance)
prompts.task: Validate that the test set genuinely proves the requirements, and that requirements remain internally consistent. Run the review and deliver findings. Rank by risk to business outcome, not by count.

prompts.name: Master – Testing & Requirements Validation
prompts.audience: Test lead and testers; business SMEs performing UAT; delivery team receiving defects
prompts.task: Support testers and the business to confirm the solution meets business needs: derive test scenarios from requirements, validate coverage, support UAT execution and review solution behaviour against intent. Produce on request
modes: UAT scenarios and scripts from pasted requirements (scenario, preconditions/data, steps, expected result, requirement ref) covering happy, negative and edge paths
coverage review flagging requirements with no scenario and scenarios with no requirement
desk check scripts for business users
defect descriptions rewritten so developers can reproduce (steps, expected vs actual, impact)
solution review checklists against original intent
inputs: SIT / UAT / DESK CHECK / BUSINESS VERIFICATION

prompts.name: BA Approach & Analysis Scope Definition
prompts.audience: PM and steering (endorsement), BA team (execution)
prompts.task: Draft the BA approach and scope so every stakeholder knows what analysis happens, when, to what depth, and why. Draft approach and scope. Challenge any area where my stated depth doesn't match its risk.
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD

prompts.name: BA Effort Estimate & Resource Forecast
prompts.audience: Resource managers and PM; finance for cost inputs
prompts.task: Estimate BA effort per package and forecast the resourcing profile over time. Draft estimates and forecast. State which packages are most likely to blow out and the early-warning sign for each.
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD

prompts.name: Master – BA Engagement Planning & Estimation
prompts.audience: Project/program manager (plan integration), resource managers (forecast), the BA team (their roadmap)
prompts.task: Define the BA approach, effort and resourcing across the project or program: analysis scope, approach and techniques per phase, estimates with assumptions, resource forecasts, and RAID inputs for the engagement. Produce on request
modes: BA approach summary (analysis needed per phase, techniques, deliverables, governance touchpoints)
analysis scope definition (in/out, depth per area, justification)
estimates (range + confidence per package, assumptions log with impact-if-wrong)
resource forecast by sprint/month with skills mix
RAID inputs specific to analysis (e.g. SME availability, requirements churn)
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD

prompts.name: Work Allocation Plan
prompts.audience: Lead BA (decision), then discussed with each BA
prompts.task: Allocate packages to BAs with explicit rationale, balanced load and managed risk. Draft the allocation. Where a stretch assignment carries delivery risk, propose the support structure that makes it safe.
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD
LIST WITH SKILL NEEDS AND EFFORT
ROLE-LABELLED BAs: LEVEL, STRENGTHS, CURRENT LOAD, DEVELOPMENT GOALS

prompts.name: BA Delivery Status Report
prompts.audience: PM or steering, per my stated cadence
prompts.task: Turn raw team inputs into an exception-focused status report the audience can act on. Draft the report. If my notes hide a risk in polite language, surface it plainly in the attention section.
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD

prompts.name: Master – BA Team Leadership & Work Allocation
prompts.audience: The Lead BA (private working documents), PM (status), individual BAs (feedback)
prompts.task: Lead and coordinate BAs across workstreams: allocate and balance work against skills and development goals, track delivery, surface risks early, and prepare fair, specific performance feedback. Produce on request
modes: work allocation plan (package → BA, rationale: skills fit, load, development; risks like key-person dependency)
delivery status report (progress by package, RAG with the reason, risks/issues, decisions needed)
load-balance review when priorities shift
performance feedback drafts (specific observed behaviours, impact, growth suggestion — never personality judgements)
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD
BAs WITH LEVELS/STRENGTHS, de-identified or role-labelled

prompts.name: Artefact Peer Review (Senior BA lens)
prompts.audience: The artefact author; review record kept for assurance
prompts.task: Review the artefact as a senior BA would: specific findings, prioritised, with rewrites — calibrated to develop the author. Run the review. Every 'blocker' must state the concrete downstream failure it would cause.
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD

prompts.name: Quality Framework & Review Cadence
prompts.audience: The BA team (daily use), governance (assurance model)
prompts.task: Define the quality framework: checklists per artefact type, review levels, and a cadence the team can sustain. Draft the framework. Justify every mandatory review step by the failure it prevents — cut any that can't be justified.
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD

prompts.name: Master – Requirements Quality Assurance & Review
prompts.audience: Artefact authors (fixes), Lead BA (assurance view), governance (sign-off evidence)
prompts.task: Review and assure the quality, consistency and completeness of BA artefacts across the engagement: define the quality bar, run reviews with specific findings, and track sign-offs. Produce on request
modes: quality checklist per artefact type (criterion, what good looks like, common failure)
artefact review (finding, location, severity, suggested rewrite; summary grade against the checklist)
cross-artefact consistency review
review cadence and sign-off tracking structure
themes-to-coach report (recurring issues across the team's artefacts, anonymised)
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD

prompts.name: Cross-Stream Dependency Register
prompts.audience: Stream leads (management), program leadership (the watch-list)
prompts.task: Build the cross-stream dependency register and expose the chains that threaten the program. Build the register from my inputs and infer likely missing dependencies from the stream scopes — marking inferred rows 'INFERRED — CONFIRM'.
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD

prompts.name: Scope Overlap Resolution & Alignment Record
prompts.audience: The two stream leads and the program forum ratifying it
prompts.task: Analyse the overlap, recommend a single-owner resolution, and draft the alignment record that prevents relitigating. Draft analysis and record. If the split option creates a fragile seam, say so plainly even if it is the politically easy answer.
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD
DESCRIBE — e.g. both streams writing requirements for the same interface

prompts.name: Master – Cross-Stream Scope & Dependency Coordination
prompts.audience: Stream leads and PMs; escalation summaries for program leadership
prompts.task: Coordinate requirements scope, dependencies and impacts across teams and workstreams: map boundaries, find overlaps and gaps, maintain the dependency register, and assess cross-stream impacts of changes. Produce on request
modes: scope boundary map (per stream: owns / consumes / explicitly not covered) with overlap and gap findings
dependency register (item, from-stream, to-stream, type, needed-by, status, risk if late)
cross-stream impact assessment for a proposed change (streams affected, requirement/artefact impacts, effort, sequencing consequence)
alignment session designs and the record of what was agreed
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD
LIST WORKSTREAMS AND THEIR SCOPE IN ONE LINE EACH
WHERE OVERLAPS OR GAPS ARE SUSPECTED

prompts.name: Escalation / Decision Paper
prompts.audience: The named decision maker; copied to the steering forum
prompts.task: Draft an escalation paper that gets a decision at first reading. Draft the paper. Strip every sentence that doesn't move the decision — then list what you cut in case I disagree.
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD
DESCRIBE, INCLUDING TECHNICAL DETAIL IF ANY

prompts.name: Steering Committee Pack Input
prompts.audience: Steering committee members reading in the 10 minutes before the meeting
prompts.task: Prepare the analysis slice of the steering pack: status they can trust, decisions framed for a yes/no, risks worth executive attention. Draft the input. Flag anything in my raw notes that a committee member would probe, with a suggested holding answer.
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD
PASTE STATUS NOTES, RISKS, DECISIONS NEEDED

prompts.name: Master – Senior Stakeholder & Sponsor Engagement
prompts.audience: Sponsors, steering committees, executive stakeholders
prompts.task: Manage alignment, escalations and decision-making with senior stakeholders and sponsors: prepare escalation papers, steering inputs, decision records and engagement summaries that respect executive attention. Produce on request
modes: escalation paper (issue, impact quantified where possible, options with consequences, the specific ask, needed-by date)
steering committee input (status headline, decisions sought with recommendations, risks worth their attention)
decision record (decision, decider, rationale, alternatives rejected, impacts)
engagement summary after key meetings (what was agreed, positions shifted, follow-ups)
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD
ROLES — e.g. sponsor, EGM, CIO — and what each cares about

prompts.name: Mentoring Plan & Development Goals
prompts.audience: Mentee (co-owner of the plan) and Lead BA
prompts.task: Draft a mentoring plan with concrete goals tied to real work, not abstract competencies. Draft the plan. If my growth areas and their aspiration conflict, name the tension and propose how to sequence both.
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD
ROLE LABEL, LEVEL, STRENGTHS, GROWTH AREAS, THEIR STATED ASPIRATION
UPCOMING WORK THAT COULD STRETCH THEM

prompts.name: Skills Gap Analysis (Team)
prompts.audience: Lead BA and resource/practice managers
prompts.task: Map the team's skills against what the engagement needs, and plan the uplift that closes delivery-critical gaps. Draft matrix and uplift plan. Single-person coverage of a critical skill is a risk even with no gap — flag those too.
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD
ROLE-LABELLED: LEVELS, RECENT WORK, KNOWN STRENGTHS/GAPS

prompts.name: Master – BA Mentoring & Capability Development
prompts.audience: The Lead BA (preparation, private) and the mentee (plans and feedback shared with them)
prompts.task: Mentor and coach BAs to lift analysis capability: mentoring plans, development goals, coaching conversation preparation, feedback drafting, and engagement-level capability building. Produce on request
modes: mentoring plan (goals from X-to-Y, activities: stretch work, shadowing, courses; check-in cadence; evidence of progress)
coaching conversation prep (opening, questions that let them self-assess first, the feedback in behaviour-impact form, agreed-actions frame)
skills gap analysis (skill, required level for the work, current evidence, gap, development route)
capability uplift actions at engagement level
inputs: PROGRAM/PROJECT, NUMBER OF BAs AND WORKSTREAMS, DELIVERY METHOD
ROLE-LABELLED — LEVEL, STRENGTHS, GROWTH AREAS, ASPIRATIONS; de-identified

prompts.name: Practice Strategy on a Page
prompts.audience: Practice sponsor (endorsement) and all practice BAs (direction)
prompts.task: Distil a practice strategy onto one page that both leadership and every practice BA can quote. Draft the page. Test each priority against 'would a BA change what they do tomorrow because of this?' — rewrite any that fail.
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
PASTE ORG STRATEGY EXTRACTS, PRACTICE PAIN POINTS, STAKEHOLDER FEEDBACK

prompts.name: Operating Model & Service Catalogue Definition
prompts.audience: Practice sponsor and PMO (agreement); delivery leaders (the customer view)
prompts.task: Design how the practice engages with delivery and formalise the service catalogue around the L3 services. Draft model and catalogue. State the failure mode of the recommended model and the guardrail against it.
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE

prompts.name: Master – BA Practice Strategy & Operating Model
prompts.audience: Practice sponsor and IT/business leadership (endorsement); the practice (direction)
prompts.task: Define the practice vision, operating model and roadmap: what role the BA practice plays in the organisation, how it engages with delivery, what services it offers, and the roadmap to get there. Produce on request
modes: practice vision and strategy on a page (vision, priorities, measures, horizon)
operating model options and recommendation (engagement model with delivery, funding model, decision rights, span)
service catalogue positioning (which L3 services lead, grow, or hold)
practice roadmap (initiatives sequenced over [HORIZON], dependencies, quick wins first)
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
WHAT'S CHANGING — org strategy, demand shifts, AI, funding

prompts.name: Playbook / Standard Draft
prompts.audience: Practice BAs at all levels; Lead BAs reviewing against it
prompts.task: Draft the playbook chapter or standard so a mid-level BA can apply it unaided. Draft it. Every MUST that lacks a named failure gets demoted to SHOULD — show me which ones you demoted.
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
TOPIC — e.g. requirements writing, process levelling (L1-L6 hierarchy), story slicing

prompts.name: Template with Embedded Quality Criteria
prompts.audience: BAs completing it; reviewers judging against it
prompts.task: Design the template: structure, per-section guidance, quality criteria, and a completed example. Draft the template. Mark sections optional-for-small-work explicitly — template bloat is the main adoption killer.
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
ARTEFACT TYPE — e.g. business needs statement, options paper, interface spec
PASTE ONE OR TWO GOOD ONES IF AVAILABLE

prompts.name: Master – Standards, Methods & Templates
prompts.audience: Practice BAs (users), Lead BAs (enforcers), governance (assurance)
prompts.task: Define and maintain BA standards, methods, templates and quality expectations: playbooks that BAs actually use, templates with embedded guidance, and method guidance matched to delivery contexts. Produce on request
modes: playbook chapters (when this applies, method steps, artefact standards, worked example, common failures)
template designs (sections, per-section guidance, embedded quality criteria, example content)
standard definitions (mandatory vs recommended, justification each)
method guidance per delivery context
adoption plan (rollout, feedback loop, retirement of superseded material)
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
WHAT EXISTS, WHAT'S MISSING, WHAT'S IGNORED
E.G. REQUIREMENTS STANDARD, PROCESS MAPPING STANDARD, AGILE ANALYSIS METHOD

prompts.name: Competency Framework (Levels & Behaviours)
prompts.audience: All practice BAs and assessors; HR for role profiles
prompts.task: Draft the competency framework: areas × levels with behavioural anchors that make assessment consistent. Draft the framework. Anchors must discriminate: if the same evidence could satisfy two adjacent levels, sharpen it — show me the cells you found hardest to separate.
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
PROPOSE FROM THE L3 CATALOGUE OR LIST — e.g. elicitation, analysis & modelling, technical analysis, agile delivery, stakeholder management, strategic advisory, AI-augmented analysis

prompts.name: Practice Capability Assessment & Development Plan
prompts.audience: Practice leadership and sponsor; anonymised summary shareable with the practice
prompts.task: Roll up individual assessments into a practice capability picture and plan the development that closes the gaps that matter. Draft heat map narrative and plan. Where assessment inputs look inflated (everyone expert), flag the calibration risk and how to fix it.
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE

prompts.name: Master – Capability & Competency Management
prompts.audience: Practice BAs (their pathway), Lead BAs (assessment), HR/leadership (workforce planning)
prompts.task: Define competency frameworks, assess capability and plan development across the practice: what each level requires, where the practice stands, career pathways, and the development plan that closes practice-wide gaps. Produce on request
modes: competency framework (competency areas × levels, behavioural anchors per cell, including emerging AI-augmented analysis skills)
capability assessment approach and practice-wide roll-up (heat map by competency, de-identified)
career pathways (level to level: what must be demonstrated, typical routes)
training and development plan targeting the practice-wide gaps
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
E.G. ASSOCIATE / BA / SENIOR / LEAD / PRACTICE LEAD
WHY NOW — growth, attrition, capability gaps, AI shift

prompts.name: Demand & Supply Forecast
prompts.audience: Practice sponsor and finance; PMO for expectation-setting
prompts.task: Forecast BA demand against supply and surface the gaps early enough to act. Build the forecast. Highlight the single most dangerous month and what must be decided now to survive it.
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
PASTE INITIATIVES: STAGE, LIKELY BA NEED, TIMING
HEADCOUNT, LEVELS, DEPARTURES, CONTRACT END DATES

prompts.name: Role Description & Onboarding Pack
prompts.audience: Candidates and recruiters (role description); the new starter and their buddy (onboarding)
prompts.task: Draft the role description and the onboarding pack that gets the hire productive fast. Draft both. Cut any 'requirement' that's really a wish — inflated musts shrink the candidate pool for nothing.
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
LEVEL AND FOCUS — e.g. Senior Technical BA

prompts.name: Master – Workforce & Resource Management
prompts.audience: Practice sponsor and finance (investment), PMO (allocation), HR (recruitment)
prompts.task: Manage BA demand, supply, recruitment and allocation across the portfolio: forecast demand, plan supply (hire/contract/develop), and prepare recruitment and onboarding materials. Produce on request
modes: demand forecast (FTE by level by month under committed/likely/possible scenarios, assumptions listed)
supply plan (current trajectory vs demand, gap analysis, response per gap with lead times and cost feel)
role descriptions (level, competencies from the framework, organisational context)
onboarding guide structure (week-by-week ramp, practice standards to learn, buddy model)
allocation principles when demand exceeds supply
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
HEADCOUNT BY LEVEL, PERM/CONTRACT MIX, KNOWN DEPARTURES

prompts.name: Practice KPIs & Maturity Assessment
prompts.audience: Practice leadership; sponsor for the performance conversation
prompts.task: Define a small honest KPI set and run a maturity self-assessment the practice can repeat yearly. Draft both. Reject any KPI I can't actually source data for — offer the nearest measurable proxy instead.
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
WHAT CAN BE MEASURED WITHOUT HEROICS

prompts.name: Improvement Initiative Charter
prompts.audience: Initiative owner and practice leadership
prompts.task: Charter the improvement initiative tightly enough that in three months we'll know if it worked. Draft the charter. If the problem evidence is anecdote-only, add a 'first, baseline it' step before the change.
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
DESCRIBE WITH EVIDENCE — metric, complaint theme, incident
WHO CAN WORK ON IT, HOW MUCH TIME

prompts.name: Master – Practice Performance & Continuous Improvement
prompts.audience: Practice sponsor (performance story), the practice (improvement ownership)
prompts.task: Measure practice performance and maturity, and drive continuous improvement: KPIs that reflect value (not activity), maturity assessment, and improvement initiatives with tracked benefits. Produce on request
modes: practice KPI set (KPI, why it matters to delivery partners, formula, source, target [PROPOSED — VALIDATE], gaming risk)
maturity assessment (dimension, level with evidence, next-level behaviours)
improvement initiative charters (problem, hypothesis, approach, benefit measure, review date)
quarterly performance narrative from my raw data
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
WHAT DELIVERY PARTNERS SAY ABOUT THE PRACTICE

prompts.name: CoP Session Plan & Topic Backlog
prompts.audience: Practice BAs; session hosts
prompts.task: Plan the next quarter of CoP sessions people choose to attend, plus the prioritised topic backlog. Draft plan and backlog. Every session must produce a takeaway artefact for the knowledge base — no takeaway, redesign the session.
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
LIST OR 'MINE FROM RECENT DELIVERY PAIN'

prompts.name: Knowledge Base Structure & Contribution Guidelines
prompts.audience: All practice BAs (contributors and searchers); curators
prompts.task: Design the knowledge base around retrieval moments, with contribution guidelines that keep quality up and duplication down. Draft structure and guidelines. Include a 'deprecation' rule — stale trusted content is worse than no content.
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
WHERE THINGS LIVE, WHAT'S FINDABLE, WHAT'S DUPLICATED
WHEN DO BAs GO LOOKING — LIST OR 'PROPOSE'

prompts.name: Master – Community of Practice & Knowledge Management
prompts.audience: Practice BAs (the community), Practice Lead (curation)
prompts.task: Foster the BA community, knowledge sharing and reuse of practice assets: community sessions people attend by choice, a knowledge base people actually search first, and lessons that change behaviour rather than filling a register. Produce on request
modes: CoP session plans (topic, format — case clinic, artefact teardown, lightning talks; prep; the takeaway artefact)
topic backlog from my pain points, prioritised by reuse value
knowledge base structure (organised by delivery context and L3 service, with contribution guidelines and quality bar for reusable assets)
lessons-learned entries rewritten from my raw material into next-time guidance, tagged for retrieval
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
WHERE ARTEFACTS AND LESSONS LIVE TODAY, e.g. Confluence spaces
WHAT KNOWLEDGE KEEPS GETTING LOST OR RE-CREATED

prompts.name: Tool / AI Capability Evaluation
prompts.audience: Practice sponsor and IT/security; the BAs who trialled it
prompts.task: Evaluate the candidate against real BA use cases and recommend adopt / trial / decline with evidence. Draft the evaluation (design before trial, findings after). Weight validation effort honestly — a tool that generates fast but validates slow may net negative.
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
LIST FROM THE CATALOGUE — e.g. meeting-notes-to-requirements, process map generation

prompts.name: AI Adoption Guidelines & Guardrails (Practice)
prompts.audience: All practice BAs; endorsed by security/privacy and the sponsor
prompts.task: Draft the practice's AI adoption guidelines: what BAs may use AI for, what they must never do, and the validation discipline that makes outputs trustworthy. Draft the guidelines. Where my organisational policy is stricter than these defaults, follow the policy and note it; where it is silent, mark the gap for the policy owner.
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE

prompts.name: Master – Tooling & AI Enablement
prompts.audience: Practice BAs (guidelines), IT/security (alignment), sponsor (investment)
prompts.task: Evaluate and embed analysis tooling and AI-enabled ways of working across the practice: tool evaluations, tooling standards, and AI adoption guidelines with guardrails that keep use safe and consistent — including the practice prompt library and G.E.T. validation discipline. Produce on request
modes: tool/AI capability evaluation (use cases served, evaluation criteria, trial design, cost model, recommendation)
tooling standards (which tool for which job, data rules per tool)

AI adoption guidelines (approved uses by task type, prohibited uses, data rules — de-identified inputs only, validation duty via Generate→Explain→Test, prompt library usage, quality scorecard for new prompts)
adoption plan with capability building (training, champions, office hours) and success measures
inputs: PRACTICE SIZE, MIX OF PERMANENT/CONTRACT, DELIVERY PORTFOLIO SHAPE
CURRENT TOOLS — e.g. Jira, Confluence, Copilot, modelling tools

prompts.name: Environment & Access Requirements Matrix
prompts.audience: Platform engineers and security reviewers
prompts.task: Define the environment set and the role-based access matrix with approval and audit requirements. Draft both tables. Flag risky patterns explicitly (shared accounts, vendor admin access, prod data in test).
inputs: WHAT DATA APPEARS IN WHICH ENVIRONMENT

prompts.name: Release Process & CI/CD Pipeline Requirements
prompts.audience: DevOps engineers (implementation) and change governance (approval)
prompts.task: Define release governance and CI/CD pipeline requirements that balance delivery speed with public-sector change control. Draft both. Note where a requirement trades speed against control and offer the option.

prompts.name: Master – Environment Access & DevOps Enablement
prompts.audience: Platform/DevOps engineers (build), security (approval), delivery teams (consumers)
prompts.task: Define the requirements for environments, access, deployment and release processes and CI/CD enablement — answering who can access which environment, how the solution is deployed, and how releases are governed. Produce on request
modes: environment requirements (environment, purpose, users, data class allowed — e.g. masked only outside prod, prod-likeness, availability window)
access matrix (role vs environment vs permission level, with approval workflow and audit needs)
deployment and runtime topology requirements
release process definition (stages, entry/exit criteria, approvals, rollback expectations)
CI/CD pipeline requirements (build, test gates, security scanning, deployment automation)

prompts.name: Interface Specification
prompts.audience: Integration designers and developers; reviewed by data owners
prompts.task: Draft a complete interface specification for designer/developer consumption. Draft the specification. Mark unknowns '[TBC — OWNER]' rather than inventing values, and list the questions that close them.

prompts.name: Migration Approach & Reconciliation Requirements
prompts.audience: Migration lead and data engineers; business owners signing off data completeness
prompts.task: Define migration scope, approach considerations and the reconciliation requirements that prove the migration succeeded. Draft all sections. Call out the riskiest entities (quality, volume, transformation complexity) and why.

prompts.name: Master – Integration, Data & Migration
prompts.audience: Integration designers, data engineers and migration teams; business data owners for validation
prompts.task: Define system integration, data movement and migration requirements: how data moves between systems, what transforms it needs, and how a migration is scoped, sequenced, validated and reconciled. Produce on request
modes: interface catalogue and specifications (interface, systems, direction, trigger, frequency/latency expectation, volumes, data payload, error handling, ownership)
source-to-target mapping with transformation rules
migration requirements (scope catalogue, migrate/archive/retire decisions, sequencing and dependencies, cutover tolerance, volume/throughput expectations)
reconciliation and validation requirements (counts, balances, sampling, acceptance thresholds)
the business-level answers to design questions (sync vs async, big bang vs phased, where transformation sits) as an options analysis

prompts.name: Monitoring, Logging & Alerting Requirements
prompts.audience: Operations engineers implementing; service management defining response
prompts.task: Define what must be monitored, logged and alerted, grounded in business impact. Draft the tables. Flag over-alerting risks and any log content that would breach privacy expectations.

prompts.name: Availability, DR & Performance Requirements
prompts.audience: Platform/infrastructure teams (design), business owners (target sign-off)
prompts.task: Define availability, disaster recovery, backup and performance requirements with business justification. Ask me the impact-of-outage questions you need, then draft. Show the cost-vs-availability trade-off where targets look expensive.

prompts.name: Master – Operational Engineering & Observability
prompts.audience: Operations engineers, platform teams, service management; business owners validating targets
prompts.task: Define monitoring, logging, alerting and operational support requirements: what needs watching, what events matter, availability and resilience needs, DR/backup expectations, and performance/scalability requirements. Produce on request
modes: monitoring requirements (what to monitor, why it matters to the business, threshold, alert severity, response expectation)
logging and audit requirements (event, data captured, retention, privacy constraints on logged personal data)
availability and resilience requirements (uptime targets by business period, failure scenarios and tolerance)
DR and backup requirements (RTO/RPO per business function with justification, recovery scenarios)
performance and scalability requirements (load, peaks — e.g. seasonal volume spikes — growth, response-time targets)
operational dashboard definitions
inputs: WHAT BREAKS FOR WHOM WHEN THIS FAILS

prompts.name: Hosting Model & Data Residency Analysis
prompts.audience: Architects (decision), privacy and security (residency confirmation)
prompts.task: Analyse hosting options (full cloud / hybrid / on-prem) and establish the data residency position. Draft the analysis. Every residency claim about a vendor/cloud service is marked '[VERIFY WITH VENDOR DOCUMENTATION]'.

prompts.name: Licensing & Consumption Model
prompts.audience: Finance and procurement (forecasting), architects (design-to-cost)
prompts.task: Model how licensing and consumption costs scale with usage so commercial decisions and forecasts are grounded. Draft the model. Never invent dollar figures; build the structure and flag every input finance must supply.
inputs: LIST WITH LICENSING BASIS IF KNOWN — PER USER, PER CORE, CONSUMPTION

prompts.name: Master – Platform Design & Infrastructure Analysis
prompts.audience: Platform architects and infrastructure engineers (decisions), finance (consumption models), governance (residency and compliance)
prompts.task: Provide the analysis that platform design decisions need: hosting model, environment strategy, compute and workload placement, network topology and connectivity, licensing and consumption modelling, and solution dependencies. Produce on request
modes: hosting model analysis (cloud/on-prem/hybrid options against data sensitivity, dependencies, latency, residency, continuity)
environment strategy (environments needed, prod-likeness, data per environment, footprint vs cost)
compute and workload placement inputs (volumes, concurrency, processing types, variability → placement considerations)
network topology and connectivity requirements (communication paths, internal/external access, partner connectivity, security boundary expectations)
licensing and consumption model (drivers, scaling scenarios, cost forecast structure)
dependency register with contract/vendor constraints
inputs: TRANSACTION VOLUMES, CONCURRENCY, PROCESSING TYPES, VARIABILITY
OTHER — EXISTING CLOUD AGREEMENTS, ON-PREM DEPENDENCIES, BUDGET

prompts.name: Security Requirements & RBAC Matrix
prompts.audience: Security architects (review), engineers (build), business owners (role sign-off)
prompts.task: Draft the security requirements and role-based access matrix for the solution. Draft requirements and matrix. Flag every place where my function list was too coarse to set permissions safely.
inputs: E.G. ENTRA ID SSO, MFA POLICY — OR 'TBD'

prompts.name: Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) Input Pack
prompts.audience: Privacy officer (assessment), project (remediation planning)
prompts.task: Assemble the structured inputs a privacy officer needs to complete a PIA efficiently. Draft the pack. List the questions only the privacy officer or legal can answer, separately from factual gaps I can close.
inputs: DESCRIBE WHAT PERSONAL/HEALTH INFORMATION IS COLLECTED, USED, STORED, DISCLOSED

prompts.name: Master – Security, Privacy & Compliance Analysis
prompts.audience: Security architects, privacy officer, compliance and audit; delivery team implementing controls
prompts.task: Ensure the solution meets security, privacy and regulatory obligations: security requirements, access management and RBAC, identity and trust, data sovereignty, privacy assessment inputs and compliance controls with audit evidence. Produce on request
modes: information classification assessment (data element, classification, handling requirements)
security requirements (authentication incl. SSO/MFA needs, authorisation, encryption at rest/in transit, logging/audit, vulnerability management)
RBAC matrix (role vs function vs permission with least-privilege and segregation-of-duties checks)
privacy assessment inputs (data flows, purposes, consent basis, retention, disclosure, cross-border touchpoints) structured for a PIA
compliance controls mapping (obligation → control → evidence) for audit
inputs: DESCRIBE, INCLUDING DATA TOUCHED AND USER POPULATIONS

prompts.name: Support Model & SLA/OLA Definitions
prompts.audience: Service management (ownership), vendors (agreement), business (expectations)
prompts.task: Define the L1-L3 support model and the SLA/OLA set for the service. Draft the model and tables. Mark targets '[PROPOSED — VALIDATE]' and flag SLA/OLA mismatches.
inputs: WHEN MUST IT WORK, IMPACT OF OUTAGE

prompts.name: Operational Readiness Checklist & Handover Pack
prompts.audience: Service transition approver (gate), support teams (receivers)
prompts.task: Produce the readiness checklist gating service transition and define the handover pack contents. Draft checklist and pack definition. Rank the items by 'pain if missing at 2am during a Sev-1' and say why.

prompts.name: Master – Service & Operational Readiness
prompts.audience: Service management, support teams, vendors and the service transition approver
prompts.task: Ensure the system, network and platform have an operational support model and are ready for production: support models, SLAs/OLAs, incident and event management, vendor responsibilities, environment governance and handover. Produce on request
modes: support model (L1-L3 responsibilities, escalation paths, hours, incident vs request flows, ITSM tool integration needs)
SLA and OLA definitions (service, measure, target, measurement method, reporting)
vendor responsibility RACI with escalation and contract reference points
service transition assessment (criteria, evidence, gaps, risk rating)
support readiness checklist and handover pack contents (procedures, known errors, FAQs, training)
inputs: INTERNAL TEAMS, VENDORS, SERVICE DESK TOOL e.g. ServiceNow
